long.text: Here is a longer piece of dictation, the kind of thing you might say into a phone while walking to a meeting. First, I want to summarize where the project stands. The audio capture is working and the speech model loads in a couple of seconds on the first launch. After that, every utterance is transcribed on the device, so nothing about my voice ever leaves the phone. Second, the text has to reach the right computer. I have two laptops and a desktop on the same private network, and I want to pick one before I speak and have the words appear exactly where the cursor is. If the network is down, the text should wait in an outbox, and I should be able to send it again with one tap. Third, I would like the whole thing to feel instant, which means holding the button, speaking naturally, and seeing the sentence appear a moment after I let go. There are a few risks. Models can use a lot of memory, long recordings may need to be split into chunks, and background noise might confuse the end of speech detection. We will measure all of that on the real phone before we decide anything else.
